content: We delight in the beauty of the butterfly, but rarely admit the changes it has gone through to achieve that beauty.
author: Maya Angelou
sourceWork: Wouldn't Take Nothing for My Journey Now (1993)
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

In Maya Angelou's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: What difficult or messy transition in your life are you currently resisting, and how might it be preparing you for your next evolution?
